newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon denies Bakassi clash with Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon denies Bakassi clash with Nigeria.

text.p: Cameroon on Wednesday denied reports in Nigerian newspapers that troops from the two neighbours fought in the disputed Bakassi peninsula last weekend.

"I have spoken to my field commanders...at the battlefront not a single gunshot has been heard for a very long time," armed forces chief of staff General Pierre Semenge told Reuters in the Cameroon capital.
Nigerian newspapers said troops fought briefly and there were no casualties on either side. They said the fighting took place at night in Nigerian villages occupied by Cameroonian gendarmes.
There was no immediate confirmation of the reports from Nigerian military authorities.
The two African nations have clashed sporadically on Bakassi, which is believed to have significant oil reserves, since 1994.
Troops of both countries are entrenched in the impoverished area whose inhabitants are mainly fishermen and speak Efik, the language of southeastern Nigeria.
Cameroon took its case to the World Court in 1994 but the court's ruling in March last year forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later.
